forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

findings.headline: Outstanding fee income from BID levy collection remains disputed and unpaid after three years of unresolved audit recommendations
findings.detail: Surrey Heath collects Business Improvement District levy from property owners and is owed collection fees, amendment fees, and debt recovery fees by the BID company. Audit recommendations from September 2023 targeting March 2024 remain outstanding. The Executive escalated the matter in November 2025 and agreed recommendations to resolve the dispute, but as of September 2026 the council and BID company are still developing a final service level agreement and awaiting completion of a Menzies audit to establish exact balances owed to the council.
findings.matters: The council has uncollected fee income owed by a significant partner after three years of negotiation, and lacks a signed service level agreement governing the arrangement, indicating challenges in enforcing fee agreements and documenting third-party partnerships
findings.figures: Outstanding monies owed (amount not specified in paper)
findings.quote: Surrey Heath Executive considered the BID Levy Arrears in November 2025 and agreed a set of recommendations which resolved the dispute.

findings.paper_title: Annex A: Audit Findings Report (ISA 260) (Grant Thornton)
findings.headline: £270k cumulative mismatch between MRP calculation schedules and general ledger identified in council's own review, indicating historical accounting errors.
findings.detail: During the Council's review of its MRP schedules, officers identified a cumulative mismatch of £270k between the MRP calculation schedules and amounts recorded in the general ledger (review covered through 2021/22). The council's review of the fixed asset register also identified assets previously excluded, raising questions about whether these were part of the funded/unfunded analysis and whether there are unidentified MRP impacts.
findings.matters: A £270k historical accounting error in MRP suggests poor financial record-keeping and control. Auditors have no assurance that the general fund position is fairly stated or whether the useable and unusable reserves are correctly apportioned.
findings.figures: £270k cumulative mismatch between calculation schedules and general ledger
findings.quote: a cumulative mismatch between the MRP calculation schedules and the MRP charged to the General Ledger of £270k

findings.paper_title: Annex A: Audit Findings Report (ISA 260) (Grant Thornton)
findings.headline: 99% of unfinanced capital expenditure assigned unrealistic 50-year useful economic lives; includes Camberley Town Centre Mall (built 1970s, purchased 2016/17) with 50-year assigned life.
findings.detail: Nearly all of the Council's unfinanced capital expenditure (99%) has been assigned a generic 50-year useful economic life. Auditors consider this unrealistic, particularly for older assets. For example, Camberley Town Centre Mall, which was built in the 1970s and purchased in 2016/17, has been assigned a 50-year horizon for MRP purposes. This deferral of charges results in low current MRP (1.2% of CFR) with charges peaking in 2066.
findings.matters: Unrealistic asset lives artificially reduce current MRP charges and overstate the benefit period of assets, allowing the council to under-provide for debt repayment. This exacerbates the already-identified MRP under-provision risk.
findings.figures: 99% of unfinanced capital expenditure assigned 50-year lives; Camberley Town Centre Mall built 1970s, assigned 50-year life
findings.quote: the adoption of the maximum 50-year useful economic lives most assets financed through borrowing (e.g, Camberley Town Centre Mall purchased in 2016/17 with a 50-year horizon despite being built in the 1970s)

findings.paper_title: Annex A: Audit Findings Report (ISA 260) (Grant Thornton)
findings.headline: £3.3m error in borrowing classification identified in prior year; loans restructured in 2024/25 resulting in £3.3m reduction to long-term borrowing with gain recognized but not verified by auditors.
findings.detail: Auditors identified a material error of £2.3m in the classification of borrowing between short-term and long-term in prior year accounts, corrected via prior period adjustment. Additionally, loans were restructured in 2024/25 resulting in a £3.3m reduction to long-term borrowing with a gain recognized in the Comprehensive Income and Expenditure Account. This amendment was made very late (9 January 2026) and auditors have not verified its appropriateness, completeness or accuracy.
findings.matters: A lender needs accurate information about borrowing maturity profile to assess refinancing risk. An unverified £3.3m adjustment to long-term borrowing made at the very end of the audit cycle raises questions about the accuracy of the council's borrowing position.
findings.figures: £2.3m borrowing misclassification in prior year; £3.3m reduction in long-term borrowing from 2024/25 restructuring
findings.quote: On the 9 January 2026, officers working with treasury advisers informed us that loans restructured in 2024/25 had not been correctly accounted for in the draft financial statements. Officers have amended the 2024/25 accounts resulting in a £3.3m reduction to long-term borrowing and a gain recognised in the Comprehensive Income and Expenditure Account. Given the late date this was highlighted, we have not verified the appropriateness, completeness and accuracy of this amendment.

findings.paper_title: Annex A: Audit Findings Report (ISA 260) (Grant Thornton)
findings.headline: Significant Weakness identified in Value for Money arrangements: auditor not satisfied council has proper arrangements for economy, efficiency and effectiveness.
findings.detail: Under the National Audit Office Code of Audit Practice, auditors must assess whether the authority has put in place proper arrangements to secure economy, efficiency and effectiveness in its use of resources. Grant Thornton has identified a significant weakness and is not satisfied that proper arrangements are in place. This finding is reported in the separate Auditor's Annual Report.
findings.matters: A VFM significant weakness is a governance red flag for lenders. It indicates the council may not be managing resources effectively and efficiently, compounding the risks already identified by the disclaimer of opinion.
findings.quote: We identified a significant weakness in the Authority's arrangements and so are not satisfied that the Authority has made proper arrangements for securing economy, efficiency and effectiveness in its use of resources.
